teams.last_evidence: Gold Cup: Canada 2-0 El Salvador, 25 Jun 2025
teams.note: Jonathan David is the strongest current Canada call and should be treated as the leading World Cup candidate. He was trusted with an in-match Gold Cup penalty against El Salvador in June 2025 and also opened Canada's shootout order in major knockout matches, which fits the wider reality that he is the senior side's main scoring reference. Cyle Larin is the clearest secondary because he remains Canada's other senior central scorer and the most natural fallback if David is absent or has already gone off.
evidence_log: 25 Jun 2025: SofaScore shows Jonathan David took Canada's in-match penalty against El Salvador in the Gold Cup; the attempt was saved before he later scored in open play.
29 Jun 2025: Canada Soccer's Guatemala quarter-final match centre lists Jonathan David as the first Canada taker in the shootout order.
5 Jul 2024: Canada Soccer's Copa America quarter-final report against Venezuela also shows Jonathan David taking Canada's first penalty in the shootout.
Current working view: David is the clearest Canada primary and strong enough now for a high-confidence World Cup label, with Cyle Larin the best fallback by seniority and striker profile.

teams.last_evidence: Concacaf Nations League Final: Mexico 2-1 Panama, 24 Mar 2025
teams.note: Raul Jimenez is Mexico's strongest current World Cup penalty candidate. The key direct evidence is his stoppage-time winning penalty against Panama in the 2025 Concacaf Nations League final, and that sits comfortably with his broader role as the senior side's most trusted central finisher in the current cycle. Santiago Gimenez is the clearest secondary because he is the other leading centre-forward in Mexico's pool and the most obvious attacking fallback if Jimenez is not the taker on the pitch.
evidence_log: 24 Mar 2025: Raul Jimenez scored Mexico's winning penalty vs Panama in the Concacaf Nations League final.
Concacaf's tournament recap also framed Jimenez as the decisive figure in Mexico's Nations League title run.
Current working view: Jimenez is the clearest Mexico primary and strong enough now for a high-confidence label, with Santiago Gimenez the best fallback in the likely tournament striker rotation.

teams.last_evidence: USMNT 3-0 Uzbekistan, 9 Sep 2023, plus 2025 Gold Cup alternate-squad evidence
teams.note: Christian Pulisic remains the strongest USA penalty candidate when the main squad is together. The freshest clean senior in-match conversion in the official trail is his penalty against Uzbekistan in 2023, while the 2025 Gold Cup showed an alternate US squad using Malik Tillman from the spot when Pulisic was absent. In full-strength A-team context, the balance of evidence still points clearly to Pulisic, with Tillman now the best named backup because he is the only other recent senior in-match taker in the file.
evidence_log: 9 Sep 2023: U.S. Soccer and SofaScore both show Christian Pulisic converted the late in-match penalty in the 3-0 win over Uzbekistan.
6 Jun 2021: U.S. Soccer's Nations League final report shows Pulisic scored the decisive extra-time penalty against Mexico in a major senior final.

30 Jun 2025: Concacaf's Gold Cup quarter-final report shows Malik Tillman took and missed the USA's in-match penalty against Costa Rica with a different tournament squad, which supports the idea that the order can change when Pulisic is absent rather than disproving Pulisic's full-strength status.
Current working view: for the likely World Cup A-team, Pulisic remains the clearest USA primary, with Tillman the best current fallback signal.

teams.last_evidence: AFC Asian Qualifiers: Australia 5-1 Indonesia, 20 Mar 2025
teams.note: Martin Boyle is the best current Australia call, but only at medium confidence because the Socceroos have used more than one taker in this cycle. The strongest recent evidence is Boyle converting the March 2025 World Cup qualifying penalty against Indonesia. Kusini Yengi is the clearest secondary because AFC also logged him taking and converting one of Australia's penalties against Palestine in 2024, which gives him the best direct fallback signal behind Boyle.
evidence_log: 20 Mar 2025: SofaScore shows Martin Boyle converted Australia's in-match penalty in the 5-1 qualifier win over Indonesia.
11 Jun 2024: AFC reported Australia had multiple penalty takers against Palestine, with Kusini Yengi converting early and Nestory Irankunda adding another late on.
Current working view: Boyle has the strongest recent claim, with Yengi the best direct backup signal from Australia's wider current-cycle penalty trail.

teams.last_evidence: AFC Asian Cup R16: IR Iran 1-1 Syria, 31 Jan 2024
teams.note: Mehdi Taremi is the clearest current Iran taker. AFC match reports show him converting the in-match penalty against Syria at the Asian Cup and then remaining Iran's central scorer through the successful World Cup qualifying run. That is enough to review the team, but it stays medium until we stack another clear recent senior in-match penalty event. Sardar Azmoun is the clearest secondary by seniority and striker profile in Iran's likely first-choice attack.
evidence_log: 31 Jan 2024: AFC reported Mehdi Taremi scored Iran's in-match penalty in the Asian Cup round-of-16 tie against Syria.
26 Mar 2025: AFC again framed Taremi as Iran's decisive scorer when qualification was sealed against Uzbekistan.
Current working view: Taremi remains the clearest first-choice signal in the Iran setup, with Azmoun the best fallback by role when Iran's main attacking core is together.

teams.last_evidence: Japan 5-0 Bahrain, 10 Sep 2024; Japan 3-1 Indonesia, 24 Jan 2024; Moriyasu designated-system quote, 30 Jan 2024
teams.note: Ayase Ueda should now be treated as one of the strongest World Cup penalty calls in the whole file. The key new context from the Japanese press is that Hajime Moriyasu moved away from the old volunteer system after the Qatar World Cup shootout loss and said he now wants to choose the order himself. Under that designated setup, Ueda has kept being trusted: he scored Japan's senior in-match penalties against Indonesia at the Asian Cup and Bahrain in World Cup qualifying, on top of the earlier El Salvador penalty and his first-kick conversion in the Tokyo Olympics shootout. Takumi Minamino remains the likeliest backup, but his biggest Japan penalty moment is still the missed first kick against Croatia in Qatar under the old volunteer system.
evidence_log: 31 Jul 2021: Soccer Digest Web reported Ayase Ueda took Japan's first shootout penalty against New Zealand in the Tokyo Olympics quarter-final and scored it.

5 Dec 2022: Gekisaka and Football Channel reported Takumi Minamino volunteered for Japan's first World Cup shootout penalty against Croatia and missed, with Moriyasu still using the old volunteer system.
30 Jan 2024: Gekisaka reported Moriyasu said he had reflected on Qatar and now wanted to move to a manager-designated penalty order rather than leaving it to volunteers.
24 Jan 2024: Japanese and AFC reporting shows Ueda won and converted Japan's in-match penalty against Indonesia at the Asian Cup.

10 Sep 2024: ABEMA Times described Ueda as Japan's 'PK kicker' when he converted against Bahrain despite heavy crowd pressure, which is strong native-language evidence that he is the designated taker.
Current working view: Ueda is Japan's nailed-on first choice and Minamino is the best backup, but Minamino's biggest national-team penalty moment remains the Qatar miss under the old system.

teams.last_evidence: AFC / SofaScore: Oman 0-3 Jordan, 5 Jun 2025
teams.note: Ali Olwan is now the clearest Jordan penalty taker. The direct evidence is strong: SofaScore shows him converting the World Cup qualifying penalty against Oman in June 2025, and he also scored from the spot in the 2025 Arab Cup quarter-final against Iraq. Mousa Al Tamari remains the biggest attacking star and the clearest fallback, but the recent penalty trail belongs to Olwan.
evidence_log: 5 Jun 2025: AFC and SofaScore show Ali Olwan converted Jordan's in-match penalty in the 3-0 World Cup qualifying win over Oman.
12 Dec 2025: SofaScore shows Olwan also scored Jordan's penalty in the Arab Cup quarter-final against Iraq.
Current working view: two late-cycle senior penalties for the same player make Olwan a strong Jordan World Cup primary, with Al Tamari the clearest challenger behind him.

teams.last_evidence: Asian Cup and World Cup qualifying trail, Jan-Mar 2024
teams.note: Son Heung-min should now be treated as a high-confidence Korea Republic primary. The Korean-language trail is stronger than the English summaries suggest: Son scored an in-match penalty against Jordan at the Asian Cup, took Korea's first kick in the shootout against Saudi Arabia, and then scored again from the spot against China in World Cup qualifying. That gives him three penalties in major competition within the first three months of 2024, with Korean reporting treating him as the designated kicker rather than a one-off taker. Hwang Hee-chan remains the right secondary because he converted against Australia in the Asian Cup quarter-final when Son won the foul.
evidence_log: 20 Jan 2024: Korean coverage of the Asian Cup group-stage draw with Jordan records Son Heung-min scoring Korea Republic's in-match penalty opener.
30 Jan 2024: Korean reporting on the Saudi Arabia round-of-16 shootout shows Son took Korea Republic's first kick and scored, which is strong pressure-order evidence.
2 Feb 2024: Son won the late penalty against Australia in the Asian Cup quarter-final and Hwang Hee-chan converted it, which remains the key secondary signal behind Son.
26 Mar 2024: AFC and Korean match reporting show Son again converted Korea Republic's in-match penalty in the 3-0 qualifier win over China PR.
Current working view: Son is Korea Republic's designated first-choice kicker, with Hwang the clearest backup when Son is not the taker.

teams.last_evidence: QFA: Qatar 1-1 North Korea, 10 Sep 2024
teams.note: Akram Afif is one of the cleanest calls on the page. He scored a hat-trick of penalties in the Asian Cup final against Jordan and then followed it with another official senior penalty against North Korea in World Cup qualifying. Almoez Ali remains the obvious secondary attacking name, but the actual penalty order is Afif until proven otherwise.
evidence_log: 10 Feb 2024: AFC and QFA both show Akram Afif scored all three of Qatar's penalties in the Asian Cup final against Jordan.
10 Sep 2024: QFA reported Afif again scored Qatar's in-match penalty in the World Cup qualifier against North Korea.
21 Dec 2024: QFA also reported Afif scored from the spot against the UAE in the Arabian Gulf Cup.
Current working view: Afif is a high-confidence World Cup primary and one of the most stable answers on the whole board.

teams.last_evidence: AFC: Saudi Arabia 1-2 Australia, 14 Oct 2025
teams.note: Salem Al Dawsari should now be treated as a high-confidence Saudi Arabia primary. The key point is not whether he scored the latest penalties but that he kept taking them in the biggest matches: he took Saudi Arabia's penalty against Indonesia, then again against Australia in another huge qualifier, and remained the designated taker even after being denied. That kind of continuity is strong hierarchy evidence. Firas Al Buraikan remains the best named fallback because he is the clearest other recent senior taker in the file, but the Saudi page should centre Salem very firmly.
evidence_log: 5 Sep 2024: wider Saudi and international match reporting showed Salem Al Dawsari took Saudi Arabia's penalty against Indonesia, with the attempt saved.
14 Oct 2025: AFC reported Salem Al Dawsari took Saudi Arabia's late penalty against Australia and Maty Ryan saved it.
8 Oct 2025: SofaScore shows Saudi Arabia won another penalty against Indonesia, but this time Firas Al Buraikan converted it.
Current working view: Salem is Saudi Arabia's designated first-choice kicker even through missed attempts, with Al Buraikan the clearest fallback if the order changes.

teams.last_evidence: Olympics 2024, WCQ 2025 and later shootout order
teams.note: Eldor Shomurodov should now be treated as a high-confidence Uzbekistan primary. The pattern is very consistent: captain, all-time leading scorer, penalty taker in historic moments, and still trusted after misses. He scored Uzbekistan's first-ever Olympic goal from the spot against Spain, then later took and missed the World Cup qualifying penalty against Kyrgyz Republic without losing status, and still led the later shootout order. Otabek Shukurov remains the best named secondary because he is the only other direct recent Uzbekistan taker in the file, but this page should be centred clearly around Shomurodov.
evidence_log: 24 Jul 2024: Shomurodov scored Uzbekistan's first-ever Olympic goal from the penalty spot against Spain.
20 Mar 2025: Championat.asia's World Cup qualifying report states Eldor Shomurodov took Uzbekistan's in-match penalty against Kyrgyz Republic and the goalkeeper saved it.
5 Sep 2025: Championat.asia's CAFA coverage shows Otabek Shukurov later converted a penalty for Uzbekistan against Kyrgyz Republic.
18 Nov 2025: SofaScore's shootout order against Iran shows Shomurodov still taking the first Uzbekistan penalty in the tiebreak.
Current working view: Shomurodov is a high-confidence Uzbekistan primary, with Shukurov the clearest named fallback rather than a true rival for the lead role.

teams.last_evidence: AFCON 2025: Algeria 1-0 Burkina Faso, 28 Dec 2025
teams.note: Riyad Mahrez is the best current Algeria penalty call. The strongest recent evidence is his AFCON 2025 winner from the spot against Burkina Faso, which restored him as the clearest direct senior signal after the more mixed 2024 period. Mohamed Amoura is the most plausible challenger from the current attacking core, but Mahrez still has the strongest national-team penalty claim.
evidence_log: 28 Dec 2025: SofaScore and Reuters/SuperSport reporting show Riyad Mahrez scored Algeria's in-match penalty against Burkina Faso at AFCON 2025.
5 Sep 2024: CAF's AFCON qualifying report against Equatorial Guinea shows Mahrez also missed an in-match penalty in a match Algeria still won 2-0.
The 2024-25 cycle was therefore mixed rather than spotless, which is why Algeria sits at medium rather than high confidence.
Current working view: Mahrez remains Algeria's clearest World Cup primary, with Amoura the most plausible challenger from the present attack.

teams.last_evidence: AFCON 2024 vs Mauritania; AFCON qualifying vs Egypt, 2024
teams.note: Ryan Mendes is one of the cleaner African calls on the board. CAF reported him scoring the late AFCON knockout penalty against Mauritania, and SofaScore later shows him converting Cabo Verde's qualifier penalty against Egypt in November 2024. Bebe remains the clearest fallback scorer in the side, but the penalty trail is firmly with Mendes.
evidence_log: 29 Jan 2024: CAF reported Ryan Mendes scored Cabo Verde's decisive in-match penalty against Mauritania in the AFCON last 16.
15 Nov 2024: SofaScore shows Ryan Mendes also converted Cabo Verde's penalty against Egypt in AFCON qualifying.
Current working view: two clean recent senior penalties for the same player make Mendes a high-confidence World Cup primary.

teams.last_evidence: AFCON 2024 vs Senegal and AFCON qualifier vs Sierra Leone, 2024
teams.note: Franck Kessie is still the best current Cote d'Ivoire answer. He took and scored the huge AFCON knockout penalty against Senegal and also converted the decisive final kick in the shootout. Later qualifier evidence against Sierra Leone showed Cote d'Ivoire using two takers in the same match, with Kessie taking the first penalty and Oumar Diakite scoring the second. That keeps the hierarchy at medium rather than high, but it still leaves Kessie as the strongest primary on both big-match status and order.
evidence_log: 29 Jan 2024: CAF and SofaScore show Franck Kessie converted Cote d'Ivoire's in-match penalty against Senegal in the AFCON last 16 and later scored the winning shootout kick.
11 Oct 2024: French-language reporting on Cote d'Ivoire vs Sierra Leone described Kessie scoring the first Ivorian penalty before Oumar Diakite added a second later in the same match.
Current working view: Kessie is still the best big-match primary, with Diakite the right secondary from the freshest qualifier evidence.

teams.last_evidence: CAF AFCON 2025: Egypt 1-0 South Africa, 10 Jan 2026
teams.note: Mohamed Salah remains Egypt's clear first-choice taker, but Omar Marmoush is the right secondary now. CAF's World Cup qualifying round-up against Ethiopia explicitly listed both players converting penalties in the same match, which is strong direct evidence of the order behind Salah when Egypt get more than one kick in a game.
evidence_log: 10 Jan 2026: Mohamed Salah scored Egypt's match-winning penalty vs South Africa in AFCON quarter-final play.
21 Mar 2025: CAF's World Cup qualifying round-up against Ethiopia listed two Egypt penalties, converted by Mohamed Salah and Omar Marmoush.
Current working view: Salah is still first, with Marmoush now the clearest secondary.

teams.last_evidence: AFCON 2024 vs Mozambique; World Cup qualifying vs Chad, 2025
teams.note: Jordan Ayew is Ghana's clear current penalty taker. CAF reported him scoring twice from the spot against Mozambique at AFCON 2024, and he then converted Ghana's World Cup qualifying penalty against Chad in March 2025. Mohammed Kudus remains the most dangerous alternative in the attack, but the penalty trail itself is firmly with Ayew.
evidence_log: 22 Jan 2024: CAF reported Jordan Ayew scored both of Ghana's in-match penalties against Mozambique at AFCON.
21 Mar 2025: CAF's World Cup qualifying round-up reported Ayew also converted Ghana's penalty in the 5-0 win over Chad.
Current working view: repeated recent senior penalties make Ayew a high-confidence World Cup primary.

teams.last_evidence: CAF AFCON 2025 Final: Senegal 1-0 Morocco aet, 18 Jan 2026
teams.note: Brahim Diaz is the clearest current Morocco primary. The deeper AFCON 2025 scan now strengthens rather than weakens that call: he took the March 2025 World Cup qualifying penalty against Tanzania, scored again from the spot against Mali at AFCON, and was then trusted with the huge late penalty in the AFCON final against Senegal ahead of Hakimi and the rest of Morocco's attack. The Panenka miss in that final was bad execution, not a hierarchy change. Hakimi remains the clearest challenger if the order shifts.
evidence_log: 25 Mar 2025: CAF match stats recorded Brahim Diaz scoring Morocco's penalty in the 2-0 win over Tanzania.
26 Dec 2025: SofaScore timeline shows Morocco again gave Brahim Diaz the penalty against Mali at AFCON and he converted it.
18 Jan 2026: CAF's AFCON final report shows Morocco again turned to Diaz for a huge late in-match penalty against Senegal, even though Edouard Mendy saved the Panenka attempt.
30 Jan 2024: SofaScore match timeline shows Achraf Hakimi took and missed Morocco's late penalty against South Africa at AFCON, which makes him the clearest alternative if the order changes.
Current working view: Diaz is Morocco's first-choice taker, and the AFCON final penalty actually strengthens that call because he was chosen for the biggest possible spot kick.

teams.last_evidence: CAF qualifiers: Senegal 1-0 Burundi, 9 Sep 2024 / South Sudan 0-5 Senegal, 7 Oct 2025
teams.note: Sadio Mane remains the best current Senegal call, but only at medium confidence. The file is mixed rather than clean: Mane scored the South Sudan qualifier penalty in November 2023, Ismaila Sarr took the penalty against Burundi in September 2024 even though Mane wanted it, and Nicolas Jackson then scored a qualifier penalty against South Sudan in October 2025. That is enough to review Senegal with Mane first and Jackson second, while stating plainly that the hierarchy is still fluid.
evidence_log: 18 Nov 2023: CAF reported Sadio Mane converted Senegal's World Cup qualifying penalty against South Sudan.
9 Sep 2024: CAF reported Ismaila Sarr took Senegal's penalty against Burundi, even though Mane wanted to take it himself.
7 Oct 2025: CAF's qualifying wrap identified Nicolas Jackson as the scorer of Senegal's penalty against South Sudan.
AFCON 2025 itself did not produce a clean new in-match Senegal penalty that settled the debate again.
Current working view: Mane is still the safest Senegal primary, with Jackson next in line, but the recent trail is mixed enough that the confidence should stay medium rather than high.

teams.last_evidence: AFCON 2025: Zimbabwe 2-3 South Africa, 29 Dec 2025
teams.note: South Africa is a mixed board once the full African cycle is included. Teboho Mokoena converted the AFCON qualifying penalty against South Sudan in November 2024, but the most recent senior in-match penalty in the file is Oswin Appollis scoring against Zimbabwe at AFCON 2025. That makes Appollis the best current lead, with Mokoena still very much in the picture rather than displaced entirely.
evidence_log: 19 Nov 2024: CAF reported Teboho Mokoena converted South Africa's in-match penalty in the 3-0 AFCON qualifying win over South Sudan.
29 Dec 2025: CAF and SofaScore show Oswin Appollis converted South Africa's later AFCON 2025 penalty against Zimbabwe.
Current working view: Appollis is the best current lead because he has the latest AFCON evidence, but Mokoena remains a live challenger rather than dropping out of the order.

teams.last_evidence: World Cup qualifying vs Malawi, 24 Mar 2025; AFCON 2025 vs Tanzania, 30 Dec 2025
teams.note: Tunisia is now strong enough for a medium reviewed call, but the hierarchy is genuinely split. Elias Achouri converted Tunisia's World Cup qualifying penalty against Malawi in March 2025, but Ismael Gharbi then took and scored Tunisia's AFCON 2025 penalty against Tanzania in December while Achouri was still on the pitch. That keeps Achouri as the best current lead on the World Cup-qualifying evidence, with Gharbi now a very strong secondary and the clearest threat to flip the order.
evidence_log: 24 Mar 2025: CAF and SofaScore both show Elias Achouri converted Tunisia's stoppage-time in-match penalty against Malawi.
31 Dec 2025: CAF reported Ismael Gharbi converted Tunisia's in-match penalty against Tanzania at AFCON 2025.
SofaScore's substitution log shows Elias Achouri only went off in the 52nd minute, so he was still on the pitch when Gharbi took the penalty in the 43rd minute.
8 Sep 2025: Tunisia beat Equatorial Guinea 1-0 through Mohamed Ali Ben Romdhane, but the winner did not come from the spot, so it did not clarify the order further.

Current working view: Achouri still has the cleaner World Cup-qualifying signal, but Gharbi's AFCON penalty while Achouri was still on the pitch is strong enough to make Tunisia a reviewed medium-confidence board rather than a holdout.

teams.last_evidence: Concacaf qualifying: Bermuda 0-7 Curacao, 9 Oct 2025
teams.note: Curacao is now strong enough for a medium reviewed call. The official Bermuda qualifier report gave the first in-match penalty to Leandro Bacuna, then later showed Jordi Paulina winning and scoring another penalty in the same match. That makes Bacuna the clearest lead and Paulina the clearest challenger, even if the full order is not completely rigid yet.
evidence_log: 9 Oct 2025: Concacaf's Bermuda report shows Leandro Bacuna scored Curacao's first in-match penalty in World Cup qualifying.
The same official report shows Jordi Paulina later won and converted another penalty in that 7-0 victory.
That same-match sequence is strong enough to stop treating Curacao as a blank or purely speculative board.
Current working view: Bacuna is a medium-confidence Curacao primary, with Paulina the clearest challenger.

teams.last_evidence: Concacaf Nations League vs Aruba, 11 and 14 Oct 2024
teams.note: Duckens Nazon is Haiti's strongest current penalty taker. The Concacaf match notes show him scoring three penalties across two Nations League matches against Aruba in October 2024, while Frantzdy Pierrot added a later penalty in the second meeting. That gives Haiti a much cleaner recent order than it first looked.
evidence_log: 11 Oct 2024: Concacaf's historical series note shows Duckens Nazon scored two penalties in Haiti's 3-1 Nations League win over Aruba.
14 Oct 2024: the same Concacaf note shows Nazon scored another penalty in Haiti's 5-3 win over Aruba, with Frantzdy Pierrot later converting one as well.
Current working view: Nazon is a high-confidence Haiti primary, with Pierrot the clearest fallback.

teams.last_evidence: Concacaf Nations League and Gold Cup, Nov 2024 to Jun 2025
teams.note: Panama is still one of the most mixed boards in Concacaf, but it is now strong enough for a medium reviewed call. Jose Fajardo scored the Nations League quarter-final penalty against Costa Rica in November 2024, Adalberto Carrasquilla then scored Panama's penalty in the 2025 Nations League final, Eduardo Guerrero converted one against Guadeloupe at the 2025 Gold Cup, and Ismael Diaz scored another against Jamaica days later. Diaz is the best current lead because he has the latest clean Gold Cup penalty, while Fajardo remains the clearest earlier knockout-stage challenger.
evidence_log: 14 Nov 2024: Concacaf reported Jose Fajardo scored Panama's Nations League penalty against Costa Rica.
23 Mar 2025: Concacaf's Gold Cup road report notes Adalberto Carrasquilla scored Panama's penalty in the Nations League final against Mexico.
16 Jun 2025: Concacaf reported Eduardo Guerrero converted Panama's penalty against Guadeloupe at the Gold Cup.
24 Jun 2025: Concacaf then reported Ismael Diaz scored Panama's penalty against Jamaica.
Current working view: Diaz is the freshest lead, Fajardo is the strongest earlier challenger, and Panama's four-taker run is now better handled as a reviewed but fluid board than as a blank holdout.

teams.last_evidence: AFA / FIFA World Cup 26 qualifying cycle review, updated Sep 2025
teams.note: Lionel Messi remains the obvious Argentina first-choice taker when available. Even without a fresh official in-match penalty logged in the current file, there is no credible competing claimant in the senior setup, and AFA still frames him as the central attacking reference and top scorer from the qualifying cycle. Julian Alvarez is now the clearest fallback because he has already converted in both Argentina's 2022 World Cup final shootout and the 2024 Copa America quarter-final shootout against Ecuador.
evidence_log: AFA's qualifying wrap records Lionel Messi as Argentina's top scorer on the road to World Cup 2026.
There is no stronger current senior evidence pointing to another first-choice penalty taker when Messi is on the pitch.

Julian Alvarez converted in Argentina's 2022 World Cup final shootout and again in the 2024 Copa America quarter-final shootout against Ecuador, which gives the backup line more real tournament evidence than before.
Current working view: Messi is still the clear Argentina primary, with Julian Alvarez the cleanest secondary if Messi is absent or substituted.

teams.last_evidence: CBF: Brazil 2-1 Colombia, 20 Mar 2025
teams.note: Raphinha is the clearest current Brazil primary after taking the March 2025 qualifier penalty against Colombia. Vinicius Junior remains the strongest challenger because Brazil had trusted him from the spot earlier in the cycle before the order appeared to tilt toward Raphinha.
evidence_log: 20 Mar 2025: CBF's qualifier report states Raphinha scored Brazil's penalty against Colombia.
Vinicius Junior had already been trusted from the spot earlier in the cycle, which keeps him as the clearest challenger rather than leaving the secondary line blank.
Current working view: Raphinha leads the Brazil order, with Vinicius Junior next in line if the hierarchy shifts again.

teams.last_evidence: FCF: Colombia 3-0 Australia, 18 Nov 2025
teams.note: James Rodriguez is still the best current Colombia call, but the hierarchy should stay at medium because it has looked genuinely disputed rather than fully locked. FCF's November 2025 report states he opened the scoring from the penalty spot against Australia, which is the freshest clean direct evidence. The wider Lorenzo-era picture is messier, though: Colombia's qualifier against Ecuador exposed James, Rafael Santos Borre and Luis Diaz all hovering around the same kick. James remains the best World Cup answer on seniority, technique and present-day evidence, while Luis Diaz stays the clearest challenger.
evidence_log: 18 Nov 2025: FCF reported James Rodriguez scored Colombia's penalty in the 3-0 friendly win over Australia.
SofaScore's event timeline confirms James as the in-match penalty taker in that match.
17 Oct 2023: Colombian reporting around Ecuador vs Colombia described a visibly disputed penalty sequence involving James Rodriguez, Rafael Santos Borre and Luis Diaz before Diaz took and missed.
Current working view: James is Colombia's strongest present-day penalty call, but the board stays medium because the hierarchy has shown real fluidity under Lorenzo.

teams.last_evidence: CONMEBOL: Ecuador 1-0 Argentina, 9 Sep 2025
teams.note: CONMEBOL reported Enner Valencia scored Ecuador's winner from the penalty spot against Argentina in the final qualifying matchday. That is strong recent first-choice evidence. Gonzalo Plata is the clearest secondary because he is the most natural attacking fallback in Ecuador's likely front line once Valencia is absent or withdrawn.
evidence_log: 9 Sep 2025: Enner Valencia scored Ecuador's penalty winner vs Argentina in World Cup qualifying.
This is strong recent senior evidence that he remains Ecuador's primary taker.
Current working view: Valencia first, Gonzalo Plata second, with Plata the strongest attacking fallback in Ecuador's likely tournament side.

teams.last_evidence: APF / Sofascore: Paraguay 2-0 Uruguay, 5 Jun 2025
teams.note: Julio Enciso is the clearest current Paraguay taker. The key point is not just that he scored against Uruguay in June 2025, but that Paraguay kept faith with him after the earlier Venezuela miss. Spanish-language reporting on that October 2024 match said Gustavo Alfaro explicitly authorised Enciso to take the penalty, which is useful hierarchy evidence in itself. Enciso then kept the role and converted the next major chance, which is exactly the pattern you want to see from a designated taker. Miguel Almiron remains the closest alternative by seniority and role, even without stronger direct penalty evidence.
evidence_log: 15 Oct 2024: Spanish-language reporting on Paraguay vs Venezuela said Gustavo Alfaro authorised Julio Enciso to take Paraguay's penalty, and Enciso missed.
5 Jun 2025: APF reported Julio Enciso scored Paraguay's penalty in the 2-0 qualifying win over Uruguay.
SofaScore's match timeline confirms Enciso as the in-match penalty taker in that same game.
Current working view: Enciso kept the job after a miss, which is strong evidence that he is Paraguay's designated first-choice taker, with Almiron the best profile-led fallback.

teams.last_evidence: Copa America 2024 shootout order vs Brazil and Canada, Jul 2024
teams.note: Federico Valverde should now be treated as a high-confidence Uruguay primary. The key evidence is not a one-off spot kick but repeated tournament pressure order: he opened Uruguay's shootouts against both Brazil in the Copa America quarter-final and Canada in the third-place match, which is the designated-trust slot in back-to-back major knockout games. Giorgian De Arrascaeta remains the right secondary from the same trusted core, while Darwin Nunez being available but unused in those shootouts matters in Valverde's favour rather than against it.
evidence_log: 6 Jul 2024: AUF and wider Spanish-language reporting on Uruguay vs Brazil show Federico Valverde took and scored Uruguay's first penalty in the Copa America quarter-final shootout.

13 Jul 2024: AUF and CONMEBOL reporting on Canada vs Uruguay again show Federico Valverde leading the order in the third-place shootout, with Giorgian De Arrascaeta also among the successful senior takers.
Darwin Nunez was available in that Copa America window but did not lead or even feature in the decisive shootout order, which is useful negative evidence for the hierarchy behind Valverde.
Current working view: Valverde is now a high-confidence Uruguay primary, with De Arrascaeta the clearest challenger from the same trusted group.

teams.last_evidence: All Whites 2024-2025 qualifying run and Fiji penalty sequence
teams.note: Chris Wood remains the obvious New Zealand primary because he is the captain, the central scorer and the focal point of the side that qualified. The clearest secondary clue comes from the Fiji qualifier, where Wood had already gone off and Ben Waine then took and missed a late penalty. That is enough to move New Zealand into the reviewed bucket at medium confidence, with Waine the best fallback name for now.
evidence_log: The All Whites' 2024-25 qualification run was built around Chris Wood as captain and main scorer.
21 Mar 2025: SofaScore shows New Zealand were awarded a late penalty against Fiji after Chris Wood had already been substituted, and Ben Waine missed it.
That Fiji sequence makes Ben Waine the clearest current fallback rather than leaving the backup slot blank.
Current working view: Wood is still the obvious World Cup primary, with Ben Waine the clearest fallback, even if the sample is not strong enough to call it a high-confidence board.

teams.last_evidence: UEFA / SofaScore: Cyprus 0-2 Austria, 15 Nov 2025
teams.note: Marko Arnautovic should now be treated as a high-confidence Austria primary. The 2025 qualifying trail is strong enough to stop hedging: he kept penalty responsibility against San Marino even after already scoring twice, then converted again against Cyprus in November, and UEFA's EURO 2024 report had him taking and scoring against Poland as well. Marcel Sabitzer is the correct secondary because Austria also trusted him with a qualifier penalty in the same campaign when the order shifted.
evidence_log: 10 Jun 2025: German-language reporting on Austria vs San Marino noted Arnautovic scored twice and still took Austria's late penalty, missing it but retaining clear first-choice responsibility.
15 Nov 2025: SofaScore shows Marko Arnautovic converted Austria's in-match penalty in the 2-0 World Cup qualifying win over Cyprus.
9 Sep 2025: German-language reporting on Austria's other Cyprus qualifier shows Marcel Sabitzer taking and scoring from the spot when the order changed.
21 Jun 2024: UEFA's EURO 2024 report states Arnautovic also scored Austria's penalty against Poland in Berlin.
Current working view: repeated competitive penalties across 2024 and 2025 make Arnautovic a high-confidence Austria primary, with Sabitzer the confirmed backup.

teams.last_evidence: SofaScore: Wales 2-4 Belgium, 13 Oct 2025
teams.note: Kevin De Bruyne is Belgium's strongest current direct penalty signal. The freshest competitive evidence is emphatic rather than thin: he scored both of Belgium's penalties in the 4-2 World Cup qualifying win away to Wales in October 2025. Belgium still stays at medium confidence, though, because the live hierarchy question is what happens when Romelu Lukaku and De Bruyne are both fully available in the same frontline. Until that is settled by a clean like-for-like match sample, De Bruyne is the best current answer and Lukaku remains the clearest challenger.
evidence_log: 13 Oct 2025: SofaScore and French-language match reporting on Wales vs Belgium show Kevin De Bruyne converted both of Belgium's in-match penalties in the 4-2 World Cup qualifying win away to Wales.
Two penalties in the same competitive match is unusually strong direct evidence in De Bruyne's favour.

The remaining caveat is still the Lukaku coexistence question, because Belgium's long-term order looked different when Lukaku was the clear focal point and the October 2025 window did not cleanly settle that scenario.
Current working view: De Bruyne is Belgium's best present-day answer, with Lukaku the clearest secondary until a both-available match proves otherwise.

teams.last_evidence: Nations League pressure-order trail plus Dalic quote, 2023-2025
teams.note: Luka Modric should now be treated as a high-confidence Croatia primary, with one important caveat: at his age, availability and minutes still matter. The deeper Croatia picture is a dual-taker system rather than a contradiction. Andrej Kramaric has taken routine competitive penalties when Modric was off or when the order was delegated, but Modric remains the designated first-choice for the biggest moments. The Dalic quote already pointed that way, and the Nations League evidence backs it up: Modric took the decisive extra-time penalty against the Netherlands, while Kramaric remains the clearest secondary when the captain is not the taker on the pitch.
evidence_log: 14 Jun 2023: Croatia's Nations League semi-final against the Netherlands showed Andrej Kramaric scoring the earlier in-match penalty before Luka Modric later converted the decisive extra-time penalty with the game on the line.
20 Mar 2025: UEFA reported Andrej Kramaric took Croatia's early penalty against France and missed.
21 Mar 2025: Croatian reporting quoted Zlatko Dalic saying Luka Modric was Croatia's first penalty taker, but he gave that France penalty to Kramaric.
9 Jun 2025: Croatian reporting on the 5-1 win over Czechia showed Modric scored Croatia's first penalty before later letting Ante Budimir take the second one.
Current working view: if Modric is on the pitch, Croatia's biggest penalties still belong to him; Kramaric is the strongest named fallback when the order shifts.

Euro 2024 quarter-final shootout vs Switzerland: Palmer took England's first penalty, Bellingham second, Saka third, Toney fourth and Alexander-Arnold fifth after Kane had already been substituted.
That order, plus Saka's Arsenal penalty role, makes Saka the clearest England backup with Palmer the strongest tertiary option.

With Griezmann retired from internationals, the backup order is less settled, but Ousmane Dembele is the strongest available secondary because he is a regular France starter and arrives with a live club-level penalty profile from PSG.

He remains the default senior taker when available; no stronger recent evidence suggests a hierarchy change.
With Antoine Griezmann out of the international picture, the backup line is less settled, but Ousmane Dembele is the strongest available secondary on current role and club-level penalty profile.

teams.last_evidence: DFB: Germany 4-0 Luxembourg, 10 Oct 2025
teams.note: Joshua Kimmich is still the best current Germany lead because he actually took and scored the World Cup qualifying penalty against Luxembourg on 10 October 2025. Kai Havertz remains the clearest alternative, but he missed the qualifying campaign through injury, which is why the live file still leans Kimmich rather than assuming Havertz would step back in immediately. Germany should still be treated as a two-name board, not a one-man answer.

Kai Havertz missed the whole qualifying campaign through injury, which is the key context around any future shift in the Germany order if he is fully fit by the tournament.
Current working view: Kimmich first, Havertz second, with Havertz fitness the main variable that could change the board before World Cup 2026.

teams.note: Granit Xhaka is Switzerland's clearest current penalty taker. Ricardo Rodriguez remains the clearest secondary because of his long-standing Switzerland penalty history and set-piece role when Xhaka is not the taker.
